:::{#thm-bernoulli-likelihood-one-group}
#### Likelihood of binary outcomes with one event probability

Let $\Outvar_1, \dots, \Outvar_n$ be mutually independent binary random variables,
each with the same event probability $\prob$:
$\Outvar_\iobs \simind \Ber(\prob)$.
For observed outcomes $\vy \eqdef (\dsn{y})$, with each $\outvar_\iobs \in \cb{0, 1}$,
the likelihood $\Lik(\prob; \vy)$ of $\prob$ depends on the data only
through the number of events $\sumin \outvar_\iobs$:

$$\Lik(\prob; \vy) = \prob^{\sumin \outvar_\iobs} (1 - \prob)^{n - \sumin \outvar_\iobs}$$

:::

::: proof

This is the solution to @exr-bernoulli-likelihood-one-group, worked in @sol-bernoulli-likelihood-one-group.

:::
